newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Oct oil exports up 15.9 pct on yr - TDB.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Oct oil exports up 15.9 pct on yr - TDB.

text.p: Singapore's domestic oil exports rose a nominal 15.9 percent year-on-year in October to Singapore $1.34 billion, the Trade Development Board (TDB) said on Wednesday.
"In volume term, it dropped by 3.9 percent," the TDB said.
The drop in volumes was partly due to the shutdown of Esso Singapore's 110,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) crude unit for about 10-days in the week ending October 11.
Also in October, Singapore Refining Co shut down its 60,000-bpd crude unit for an unscheduled one-week maintenance.
The increase was down from the 26.3 percent year-on-year hike chalked up in September which amounted to $1.31 billion.
"Oil domestic exports recorded a double digit growth...to reach $1.3 billion in October 1996 as (the) oil price continued to rise", TDB said.
